status: Staged fact sheet for PSPMAN 0.1.0-alpha.6 User's Guide

identity.creator: ObsoleteSony
identity.description: Walkman-inspired FLAC and MP3 music player for Sony PSP, built with PocketJS.
identity.sourceAvailability: Private-source during active development; source code is not included with the Public Alpha

installation.storage: PSP storage; Memory Stick, Memory Stick Micro (M2), and PSP Go internal system storage where applicable

hardware.softwareRequirement: Custom firmware or another working homebrew environment

audio.supported: stereo 16-bit / 44.1 kHz FLAC; MPEG-1 Layer III MP3 at 44.1 kHz, CBR or VBR, mono or stereo, through 320 kbps

metadata.flac: Vorbis comments and embedded PICTURE front cover
metadata.mp3: ID3 title, artist, album, track, and disc fields with embedded APIC JPEG or PNG front cover
metadata.display: UTF-8 metadata is preserved; Alpha 6 substantially expands practical Japanese and mixed-script glyph coverage

artwork.behavior: Unsupported or damaged embedded artwork may fall back to No Cover without interrupting playback; same-track reselection republishes already loaded artwork correctly
artwork.guidance: Embedded JPEG or PNG; use smaller JPEG artwork as a temporary workaround when PNG or unusually large artwork does not display

library.startup: recursively scans enabled storage roots and reuses the persisted library index

spectrum.behavior: Visualizes live PCM without changing the sound
spectrum.paletteMemory: Remembered while PSPMAN remains open; resets to Classic after the application exits; independent from Cassette colors

about: SELECT opens the global About overlay; the PSP system Back button closes it
diagnostics: Pause playback, return to Library, then hold TRIANGLE to open Diagnostics
quit: HOME opens the PSP system confirmation; a confirmed exit completes PSPMAN's clean shutdown path

controls.buttonAssignment: PSPMAN follows the PSP system Cross/Circle confirm assignment automatically; there is no PSPMAN override

lyrics: Optional local synchronized UTF-8 .lrc sidecars beside MP3/FLAC; loaded on demand and never downloaded online
playbackSpeed: 1.0x, 1.25x, 1.5x, 1.75x, 2.0x with pitch preservation; global selection persists
